newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian cargo craft takes oxygen reserves to Mir.
newsitem.headline: Russian cargo craft takes oxygen reserves to Mir.

text.p: An unmanned Russian cargo craft docked with the Mir orbiting station on Tuesday, taking oxygen reserves and equipment to two Russian cosmonauts and a U.S. astronaut to help them repair their air supply system.
"The craft docked automatically with Mir at 9.30 p.m. (1730 GMT) without any problems," an official said by telephone from mission control in the town of Korolyov near Moscow.

The Progress-34 craft blasted off last Sunday with 50 kg (110 lbs) of pure oxygen, as well as tools and parts for repairs to the on-board oxygen-making equipment damaged by leaks to Mir's cooling system.
U.S. space officials said last Friday the leaks had knocked out a device used to maintain breathable air on board, although backup systems were running.

The latest in a series of problems in Russia's cash-strapped space programme prompted a NASA official to say the U.S. space agency would review safety on Mir before sending any more astronauts to live and work there.
The 11-year-old space station's problems include a brief but intense fire which broke out during use of the back-up oxygen supply last month.
NASA's shuttle-Mir programme director, Frank Culbertson, said last week the space station was showing its age but he was confident the Russians would keep it operating.
"Right now it looks very positive. Unless there were some other failures, there is almost no likelihood we would change our plans," he said.
The Progress is also carrying food, scientific equipment, laundry and cleaning materials and presents from the relatives of those on board.
The crew is expected to begin unloading the supplies on Wednesday.
